what_its_for: Ertapenem is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections in different parts of the body, including the stomach, lungs, skin, urinary tract, and pelvis. It is also used to prevent infections after certain bowel surgeries. It works by killing the bacteria causing your infection.
how_to_take: Ertapenem is given as an injection either into a vein (IV) or into a muscle (IM). A healthcare provider, nurse, or home health aide will give you this medicine. If you are using it at home, your doctor or nurse will teach you how to prepare and give the injection properly. Always follow the exact instructions you were given. Never inject this medicine yourself unless you have been fully trained to do so. Use each vial only once and throw it away after use, even if there is medicine left inside.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 1 gram (1,000 mg) given once daily. For children between 3 months and 12 years old, the dose is based on body weight and is usually given twice daily. Your doctor will decide the right dose and how long you need to take this medicine based on the type and severity of your infection. Most treatment courses last 3 to 14 days. Do not stop taking it early even if you feel better, unless your doctor tells you to.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, give it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not give two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist for guidance.
storage: Store unmixed vials at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep them in a dry place away from light. After mixing (reconstitution), the solution must be used within 6 hours if kept at room temperature, or within 24 hours if stored in the refrigerator (2°C to 8°C or 36°F to 46°F). Do not freeze the mixed solution. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of used needles and syringes safely in a puncture-resistant sharps container.
what_to_avoid: Avoid mixing ertapenem with other medications in the same IV bag or syringe unless specifically instructed by your pharmacist or healthcare provider. Do not use dextrose (glucose) solutions to dilute this medicine. Avoid drinking alcohol or taking herbal supplements without first checking with your doctor or pharmacist, as these may affect your treatment. Tell all your doctors and dentists that you are using this antibiotic before any procedure.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: severe allergic reaction signs such as hives, rash, swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat, or difficulty breathing; severe or bloody diarrhea, stomach cramps, or fever (which may be a sign of a serious gut infection called C. diff); seizures or convulsions; confusion, agitation, or unusual changes in behavior; pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site; yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); or signs that the infection is not improving or is getting worse after a few days of treatment.
when_it_works: You may start to feel better within a few days of starting ertapenem. However, it is very important to finish the full course of treatment your doctor prescribed, even if you feel completely better before it is done. Stopping too early can allow the bacteria to come back and become harder to treat.
special_populations: Kidney problems: If you have reduced kidney function, your doctor may lower your dose or adjust how often you receive it. Always tell your doctor about any kidney problems before starting this medicine. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Your doctor will weigh the benefits and risks before prescribing this medicine during pregnancy. Small amounts of ertapenem may pass into breast milk, so discuss this with your doctor. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects, especially effects on the kidneys and nervous system. Your doctor may check your kidney function more closely. Children: Ertapenem can be used in children 3 months and older, with doses adjusted for body weight. It is not recommended for infants younger than 3 months.
